newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end mixed, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed in slow trade on Thursday.
Traders said that as the domestic A share markets had slumped and new A share issues had slowed in the past two weeks, repo rates were kept in a narrow range for lack of stimulus.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract rose to 8.30 percent from 8.00 percent on Wednesday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market fell to 1.4 million lots from 1.8 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Most institutions stood on the sidelines on Thursday on the absence of fresh market-moving news," one trader said. "This made the repo rates move in a narrow range on thin volume."

Traders said China's falling inflation rate this year was another reason for the quiet trading, which was likely to depress repo rates in the mid-term and make investors unwilling to build long-term positions.
Traders said they believed a new A share issue on the Shenzhen stock exchange would give the repo rates some support on Friday.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Thursday amid strong sentiment after rises in the past two weeks with liquidity continuing to flow into the spot market from the weak stock markets, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose slightly to 110.90 yuan from 110.62 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose slightly to 1.09 million lots from 1.04 million lots.
Traders said they expected the spot market to have see technical corrrection shortly.
